learning_outcomes.text: Knows the structure and content of the Road Code and the Implementing Regulations, with applicability in the field of transport and road safety.
Understands the meaning of road signs, markings, and signals specific to vehicle traffic.
Recognizes the types of offenses and contraventions stipulated by road legislation, as well as the corresponding sanctions.
Knows legislative aspects related to the circulation of special or autonomous vehicles and their involvement in road safety.
Understands the role of road legislation in the design and implementation of mechatronic systems in vehicles (e.g., ADAS systems, automatic braking, automatic signaling, etc.).
Is able to correctly interpret road regulations in specific situations and apply them in a technical or road context.
Correctly analyzes traffic signs and priority rules, both in standard and atypical scenarios.
Uses interactive learning tools (quizzes, simulators) for self-assessment of road legislation knowledge.
Proposes technical-legislative solutions in practical scenarios (e.g., behavior of automatic systems in cases of non-compliance with rules).
Correlates legal regulations with technological requirements of intelligent driver assistance systems.
Demonstrates responsibility in applying traffic rules and correctly interpreting legislation in specific activities of the field.
Demonstrates autonomy in studying and deepening legislative norms applicable in the field of vehicles and road safety.
Assumes legal and professional responsibility in the analysis of simulated or real road events.
Respects ethical, safety, and social responsibility principles in using road legislation knowledge.
Is able to assess risks and make correct legal decisions in interdisciplinary contexts (technical and legal).

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades will be awarded as whole numbers from 1 to 10, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. The Colloquium (60% of the final grade) includes a formative evaluation test (40% of the Colloquium grade) and a summative evaluation test (60% of the Colloquium grade). The Seminar activities (40% of the final grade) include active participation, homework (50% of the Seminar grade), and an evaluation test (50% of the Seminar grade).
